body:
🟠📝 **Fix · docs: Acceptance criterion uses a 0.6 s section, but sections must be at least 1 s**

Line 340 says sections are at least `WEBCAM_MIN_SEGMENT_SECONDS` (1 s) long, and `startSectionAt` is refused when the window is under 1 s (line 388). That makes the criterion "A 0.6 s section with a 1000 ms transition animates for 300 ms" impossible to set up, so nobody can check it. Use a section that can exist and still hits the cap, for example "a 1.2 s section with a 1000 ms transition animates for 600 ms". Failure 3 at line 156 already does this with a 1 s section.

🟠📝 **Fix · docs: `webcamStateAt` formula mixes milliseconds and seconds**

`ms` is in milliseconds (line 316, 100–2000), but `s`, `e` and `t` are source seconds (line 323). As written, `d = min(ms, (e − s) / 2)` almost always picks the half-section in seconds, and `p = ease((t − s) / d)` divides seconds by a value that may be either unit. Step 3 (line 360) has the same problem. Spell the conversion out, for example `d = min(ms / 1000, (e − s) / 2)`. This is the spec the implementation and the failure-1 and failure-3 tests will be written from.

🟡📝 **Consider · docs: Open-input bound differs between failure 19 and section 4.5**

Section 4.5 (line 575) says inputs open at an item's start and are disposed at its end, "so at most two are open at once". Failure 19 asserts at most `maxConcurrentVideos + 1`. Acceptance (line 256) says "one input per visible item". Pick one bound. If the +1 is meant for pre-opening the next item, as the preview does by mounting 1 s early, say so in 4.5. Otherwise the test will allow a leak that the design rules out.

🟡📝 **Consider · docs: Split is not visually a no-op when the 50 % cap changes the left half's transition**

The spec claims that splitting changes nothing visually. The right half does draw the same, because its from equals its to. The left half does not always: it keeps the transition, but its effective duration is `min(ms, 50 % of the section)` (decision 3), and the section is now shorter. For example, a 2 s section with a 1000 ms slide split at +1.5 s plays a 750 ms slide instead of 1000 ms. Either state this or say how split preserves the original effective duration.

🟡📝 **Consider · docs: Video limit check doesn't cover restoring a hidden media lane**

`concurrentVideoCount` counts only visible lanes, and refusal is defined only for placing, moving or trimming an item. Restoring a hidden lane through "+ Add track" (`setMediaLaneHidden`, open question 8) can bring back video items that push the count past 2 at some instant. Say whether that restore is refused with the same message, or what happens instead. Failure 15's test should cover the restore path too.

This criterion can't be tested. §2.1 says sections are at least `WEBCAM_MIN_SEGMENT_SECONDS` (1 s) long, so a 0.6 s section can't exist, and `startSectionAt` and split would both refuse to create one. Failure 3 already uses a valid case (a 1 s section with a 2000 ms request animates for 500 ms). Use a section of 1 s or longer here too, for example "A 1.2 s section with a 1000 ms transition animates for 600 ms".

Two hidden segments that touch are covered, but two that are close aren't. When the gap between them is under 400 ms, the fade-in after the first and the fade-out before the second overlap, and step 5 doesn't say how to combine them. The choice changes what renders. With `max`, opacity jumps from 0 straight to about 0.45 when a 100 ms gap starts, so the fade pops. With `min` (or a product), it stays continuous. State the combination rule (`min` keeps it continuous) and add the case to failure 6 so the test covers it.

The limit is only checked when an item is placed, moved or trimmed, and `concurrentVideoCount` only counts visible lanes. So un-hiding a media lane bypasses it: `setMediaLaneHidden`, or restoring the lane from "+ Add track", can bring back a video that overlaps two visible ones. The §6 parser doesn't check the limit either. Then the preview and the export run three decoders, which is exactly what failures 15 and 19 rule out.

<details><summary>Technical details</summary>

````markdown
# Concurrent-video limit can be bypassed by un-hiding a lane

## Affected sites
- specs/2026-10-31-editor-timeline-v2-design.md §4.4 (limit enforced only on place/move/trim)
- §4.1 edit list: `setMediaLaneHidden` has no refusal rule
- §3.1: "+ Add track" restores hidden media lanes
- §6: `mediaLanes` parsing clamps numbers but does not check concurrency
- failure 15 / failure 19, acceptance "A third video visible at the same instant is refused"

## Required outcome
- Every path that can make a lane visible either keeps `concurrentVideoCount(lanes, T) ≤ 2` for all `T` or says what happens when it doesn't (refuse the un-hide with the same reason, or keep the lane hidden on load).
- The export side states that `maxConcurrentVideos` also holds for sessions loaded from disk.
````

</details>

Calling the split "visually nothing" only holds for the right half. The left half is shorter now, so its effective duration `min(ms, len / 2)` can shrink. Splitting a 2.5 s section that has a 1000 ms slide at 1.2 s gives a 600 ms slide, and the striped band gets narrower. The default 400 ms is never capped, because sections are at least 1 s, but any `ms` over 500 is. Either accept this and say so (as the cut-through-a-transition case already does), or have split refuse or clamp so the left half keeps its effective duration.
